nodes.description: Acral anhidrosis from loss of sudomotor innervation, demonstrable as an absent sympathetic skin response or absent sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex testing. Note that the two cited sources disagree on the direction of the sudomotor abnormality: the comparative HSAN assessment reports acral anhidrosis, while GeneReviews lists hyperhidrosis among the variable autonomic disturbances. Both are curated rather than reconciled, because nothing in either source resolves the discrepancy.

nodes.description: Autonomic involvement that is real but milder and more variable than in familial dysautonomia: acral anhidrosis, tonic pupils, eating and swallowing difficulty, constipation, episodic fever, hypotonia and episodes of apnoea. The autonomic ganglion neurons are lost by the same mechanism as the sensory ones, which is why the autonomic features track the sensory ones rather than forming a separate disease axis.

nodes.description: The three HSAN2 gene products converge on the intracellular logistics of the sensory neuron. KIF1A transports synaptic vesicle precursors down the axon and physically interacts with the domain encoded by the HSN2 exon of WNK1; RETREG1/FAM134B maintains cis-Golgi structure. The convergence, rather than any one gene's individual function, is the argument that HSAN2 is one mechanistic entity: the sensory neuron has an exceptionally long axon and is correspondingly intolerant of defects in cargo transport and secretory-pathway organization.

nodes.description:
The rate-limiting lesion of the disorder: reduction or absence of peripheral sensory neurons. The primary lesion is at the cell body: dorsal root ganglion neurons are reduced or absent, rather than surviving while their distal axons die back. That is what makes the deficit multimodal, affecting large and small fibres alike rather than being pain-selective.
It does NOT make the deficit anatomically uniform. GeneReviews reports the sensory deficit as predominantly distal with the lower limbs more severely affected, so cell-body loss and a distal clinical gradient coexist here. An earlier revision of this entry claimed the deficit was "universal rather than distally graded" and used that to justify declining module conformance; the distribution claim was wrong, and the conformance decision is re-argued in `notes` on the correct basis.

nodes.description: A biallelic truncating or loss-of-function variant in one of three genes required for the long-term maintenance of dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons: the nervous-system-specific HSN2 exon of WNK1, RETREG1/FAM134B, or KIF1A. Two of the three are restricted to alternatively spliced, nervous-system-specific exons, which is what makes the resulting disease a pure sensory neuronopathy rather than part of the multisystem phenotype those genes' other isoforms produce.

nodes.description: Severe impairment of pain, temperature, touch and vibration perception involving both large and small fibres, present from infancy and distally predominant with the lower limbs affected before the upper. Sensory nerve conduction is highly abnormal while motor conduction studies are almost normal — the electrophysiological dissociation that identifies the disorder as a pure sensory neuronopathy.

nodes.description: The destructive clinical terminus. Because injury is not felt, repeated unrecognized trauma to fingers and toes produces trophic ulcers, osteomyelitis, painless fractures, neuropathic joints and progressive acro-osteolysis, ending in autoamputation of digits. The mutilation is mechanically driven and preventable in principle by protection and surveillance, which is what makes the absence of disease-modifying therapy less absolute than it appears.

nodes.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. Management is protective: surveillance and care of the extremities, protective footwear and orthoses, prompt treatment of ulcers and osteomyelitis, and dental measures where tongue and lip biting occurs. Because the mutilation is mechanically driven rather than intrinsic to the neuronal loss, this is the intervention that most changes outcome.
